tasks.analysis: Many animals rely on internal biological clocks to coordinate their behavior with environmental changes. These clocks allow organisms to detect variations in day length and adjust their physiology accordingly. As daylight increases, signals from the nervous system trigger the release of hormones that regulate processes such as growth, reproduction, and migration. These hormonal changes lead to observable shifts in behavior, including increased activity levels and seasonal breeding.
